expectations.text: Review names Cynefin domain as Complicated (or Clear — both defensible)
expectations.evidence: No Cynefin framework or domain classification appears anywhere in the review. Baseline lacks the framework.

expectations.text: Review selects Quick tier (sub-day appetite, no one-way door auto-fire)
expectations.evidence: No tiering (Quick/Full) framework invoked. Review proceeds at uniform depth without selecting a tier.

expectations.text: B2 (scope) verdict is SUSTAINED — concern that 'unused' is unverified
expectations.evidence: No B2 bucket or SUSTAINED/OVERTURNED verdict scheme. Review does flag '"Unused" is unverified' as gap #2 and concern #1, but lacks the structured B2 verdict the assertion requires.

expectations.text: Falsifying condition for B2 is concrete (e.g., grep for PrizeCategorySelector references)
expectations.evidence: 'static analysis result (e.g. knip, ts-prune, ripgrep across app/, spec/, test/, stories/, server templates, i18n keys, dynamic-component registries)' — concrete tools and paths named.

expectations.text: Final recommendation is REVISE (not APPROVE — scope claim unverified)
expectations.evidence: 'Recommendation: Do not approve as written. Send back for a 30–60 minute reshape... Reshape, don't rebuild.' — functional REVISE verdict.

expectations.text: Review does NOT inflate to Full tier (would be over-review for a one-day reversible change)
expectations.evidence: Review is moderately sized (~50 lines), proportionate to a one-day plan; does not escalate to deep architecture/dependency analysis. No tier framework so cannot 'inflate to Full' but stays appropriately scoped.

eval_feedback: Assertions 1, 2, 3 are framework-bound (Cynefin, tier, bucket-numbered verdict) and necessarily fail without the skill — they discriminate well between with/without but offer no credit for functionally equivalent reasoning in the baseline (e.g., baseline does flag 'unused' as unverified, just not under a B2 label). This is by design but worth noting.
